introduce: Lie on your right side with your forearm supporting your body. Hold your body in a straight line. \n\nThis exercise targets the abdominal muscles and obliques.
name: SIDE PLANK RIGHT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your arm at a 90 degree angle.
Keep your elbow directly under your shoulder.
Open your chest.
Always keep your body straight.
Put pressure on your wrist and elbow.
Don't put pressure on your shoulders.
Breathe regularly.
To make it easier, put your top foot forward on the mat.
Your abdominals will be burning, maybe even shivering.
Your shoulder should not be sore.
This exercise can strengthen your core.

introduce: Run in place while pulling your knees as high as possible with each step. \n\nKeep your upper body upright during this exercise.
name: HIGH STEPPING

tips.text: Keep your upper body straight.
Do it as fast as you can.
Don't bend your back.
Breathe naturally.
To make it harder, raise your knees as high as you can.
If you feel it's too hard, slow down.
You can feel your heartbeat quickening.
This is a great exercise for your lower body.
This cardio exercise can strengthen your heart and lungs.

introduce: Lie on your left side with your forearm supporting your body. Hold your body in a straight line. \n\nThis exercise targets the abdominal muscles and obliques.
name: SIDE PLANK LEFT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your arm at a 90 degree angle.
Keep your elbow directly under your shoulder.
Open your chest.
Always keep your body straight.
Put pressure on your wrist and elbow.
Don't put pressure on your shoulders.
Breathe regularly.
To make it easier, put your top foot forward on the mat.
Your abdominals will be burning, maybe even shivering.
Your shoulder should not be sore.
This exercise can strengthen your core.

introduce: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and your hands on your hips. \n\nStep a big step backward with your right leg and lower your body until your left thigh is parallel to the floor. Return and repeat with the other side.
name: BACKWARD LUNGE

tips.text: Take a big step backward.
Keep your legs at a 90 degree angle.
Keep your weight on your heels when pushing your body up.
Don't let your front knee go past your toes.
Inhale when you go down, and exhale when you go up.
To increase the difficulty, hold a dumbbell in your hands.
Your knees should not be sore.
This targets all your leg muscles.
It\'s a good leg exercise that won\'t hurt your knees.

introduce: Stand with your left hand lifted overhead and right hand on your waist. \n\nBring your left elbow and left knee to meet each other. Stretch out and repeat.
name: STANDING OBLIQUE CRUNCHES LEFT

tips.text: Try not to let your lifted feet touch the ground.
You can hold a wall or chair to keep balance.
Exhale when crunching, and inhale when stretching out.
Do it slowly to fully stimulate your obliques.
Please keep your hips in place.

introduce: Stand with your right hand lifted overhead and left hand on your waist. \n\nBring your right elbow and right knee to meet each other. Stretch out and repeat.
name: STANDING OBLIQUE CRUNCHES RIGHT

tips.text: Try not to let your lifted feet touch the ground.
You can hold a wall or chair to keep balance.
Exhale when crunching, and inhale when stretching out.
Do it slowly to fully stimulate your obliques.
Please keep your hips in place.

introduce: Start on all fours. Exhale as you lift your hips into an inverted ‘V’ shape, and lengthen your spine.\n\nAlternately lift and lower your heels with steady breath.
name: WALK THE DOG

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Relax your neck.
Keep a steady and even breathing rhythm without holding your breath.
Notice the elongation from your fingertips to your sit bone.
Draw your shoulders away from your ears.
Please press all areas of the palms equally on the floor.
This exercise stretches your shoulders, hamstrings, calves, and arches.

introduce:
Lie flat on your back with your legs extended and your arms resting by your sides.

Extend your legs toward the ceiling. Engage your core muscles to lift your shoulders off the mat. Hold your right ankle with both hands. Lower your left leg at an angle.

Pull your right leg once. Switch legs and repeat the exercise.
name: SINGLE STRAIGHT LEG STRETCH

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please keep your pelvis and trunk stable.
Please keep your legs straight.
You can adjust the angle of your leg and the position of your hands on your leg.
This exercise challenges the abdominal muscles.
This exercise can stretch the hamstring muscles of the back of the thighs.
Exhale as you lift your shoulders off the mat and pull one leg towards you.
Inhale as you switch legs, keeping the core engaged and the upper body lifted.
